x: The Maukhari dynasty originated at Gaya in Bihar, where its earliest inscriptions are found. The family later ruled from Kannauj.
t: Discriminate the place of origin from the later capital.

x: The Maukhari line ran Harivarma, Adityavarma, Ishvaravarma, Ishanavarma, Sharvavarma, Avantivarma and Grahavarma. Among the four listed, the order is Harivarma, Ishvaravarma, Sharvavarma, Grahavarma, giving B, D, A, C.
t: Recall the Maukhari succession from founder to Grahavarma.

x: I and II are correct: rulers of 20 countries, Brahmins, Shramanas and courtiers attended the Kannauj Assembly of 643 AD. III is false because the Prayagraj Sangam hosted the Mahamoksha Council, not the Kannauj Assembly.
t: Discriminate the Kannauj Assembly from the Prayag assembly.
s:
Consider the following statements about the Kannauj Assembly:
I. Rulers of 20 countries attended it.
II. Brahmins and Shramanas attended it.
III. It was held at the Prayagraj Sangam.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The Kannauj Assembly was attended by rulers of 20 countries, Brahmins, Shramanas and courtiers; the Mahamoksha Council met at Prayagraj Sangam; Hiuen Tsang was the Chinese traveller; Harshacharita is the main source, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Link each event or source to its place or person.

x: Harsha held the Mahamoksha Council at the Prayagraj Sangam once every fifth year, distributing his accumulated wealth in charity. Hiuen Tsang attended the sixth such assembly.
t: Recall the interval of Harsha's Prayag assembly.

x: Harshacharita was written by Banabhatta, the court poet of Harsha, who also wrote Kadambari. Hiuen Tsang wrote the Si-yu-ki, and Al-Masudi was an Arab traveller.
t: Link the text to Harsha's court poet.

x: Hiuen Tsang set out from China in 629 AD and reached India during Harsha's reign, staying for many years. 836 AD is the date of Mihir Bhoja's capture of Kannauj, a common trap.
t: Anchor Hiuen Tsang to Harsha's reign in the 7th century.
s: Hiuen Tsang set out on his journey to India in:

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the Narmada, and this conflict is recorded in the Aihole Inscription and by Hiuen Tsang. R names the sources, not the cause of the defeat.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A or only its source.

x: Harsha's original base was Thanesar, he shifted his capital to Kannauj, he was defeated by Pulakesin II on the Narmada, and the Mahamoksha Council met at Prayagraj Sangam, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall the place linked to each stage of Harsha's reign.

x: Option B is incorrect: the Tripartite Struggle was fought for control of Kannauj, not Ujjain. Kannauj became the prize after Harsha, was called Mahodaya or Mahodayashri, and the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas fought over it.
t: Recall the object of the Tripartite Struggle.

x: All three are correct: in the 8th–9th century CE, the Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas fought the Tripartite Struggle to control Kannauj.
t: Check the period, the powers and the aim separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Tripartite Struggle took place during the 8th–9th century CE.
II. The Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas were the three powers involved.
III. Its objective was control of Kannauj.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Nagabhata I founded the imperial Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty in the 8th century and resisted the Arabs. Vatsaraja and Mihir Bhoja were later rulers, and Mahipala was a Pala and Pratihara name.
t: Discriminate the founder from later Pratihara rulers.

x: The Pratiharas first ruled from Ujjain and later from Kannauj; Mihir Bhoja took the titles Adivaraha and Prabhasa and followed Vaishnavism, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall each Pratihara capital and Mihir Bhoja's titles.

x: Both are true: the Arab merchant Suleman described Mihir Bhoja as ruler, and Al-Masudi called the Pratihara kingdom Al-Juzr and its king Baura.
t: Check each Arab writer's description separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Suleman identified Mihir Bhoja as the ruler.
Statement B: Al-Masudi referred to the Pratihara kingdom as Al-Juzr and Bhoja as Baura.

Which of the following is correct?

x: The Pratihara order is Vatsaraja, Nagabhata II, Mihir Bhoja, Mahendrapala I and Mahipala. The four listed therefore run C, D, A, B.
t: Arrange the Pratihara rulers in order of succession.

x: Three are correct: Kannauj was the Maukhari capital, was called Mahodaya or Mahodayashri, and became the later Pratihara capital. Statement 4 is false because the Mahamoksha Council met at Prayagraj Sangam.
t: Check each statement about Kannauj separately.

x: Adityavarma was an early Maukhari ruler. Harshavardhana belonged to the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty, while Mihir Bhoja and Nagabhata I were Gurjara-Pratiharas.
t: Discriminate Maukhari rulers from Pushyabhuti and Pratihara rulers.

x: Mihir Bhoja captured Kannauj around 836 AD and made it the Pratihara capital. 629 AD relates to Hiuen Tsang's journey.
t: Place Mihir Bhoja in the early 9th century.

x: Pushyamitra Shunga killed the last Mauryan king, Brihadratha, around 185 BC and founded the Shunga dynasty. Devabhuti was the last Shunga, and Susharma the last Kanva.
t: Recall which dynasty the Shungas replaced.

x: Simuka, founder of the Satavahana dynasty, is said to have overthrown Susharma, the last Kanva ruler. Devabhuti was the last Shunga ruler, removed by Vasudeva Kanva.
t: Recall the last ruler of each dynasty before the next.

x: Pushyamitra replaced Brihadratha Maurya, Vasudeva Kanva replaced Devabhuti, Simuka replaced Susharma, and the Sthanakvasi sect grew out of the Lonka sect, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Link each founder to the predecessor he replaced.

x: Vijayanagara was ruled by the Sangama (from 1336), Saluva (1485), Tuluva (1505) and Aravidu (1570) dynasties in turn, giving B, D, C, A.
t: Arrange the Vijayanagara dynasties by year.

x: Each dynasty's predecessor: Khalji after Slave, Tughlaq after Khalji, Sayyid after Tughlaq, and Lodi after Sayyid, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the order of the Delhi Sultanate dynasties.
s:
Match each dynasty in List-I with its immediate predecessor in List-II:

List-I
(a) Khalji Dynasty
(b) Tughlaq Dynasty
(c) Sayyid Dynasty
(d) Lodi Dynasty

List-II
(i) Sayyid Dynasty
(ii) Slave Dynasty
(iii) Tughlaq Dynasty
(iv) Khalji Dynasty

x: Harsha began at Thanesar but made Kannauj his capital after taking over the Maukhari kingdom. Thanesar is the trap, being his original base.
t: Separate Harsha's original base from his later capital.

x: The Nanda dynasty replaced the Shishunaga dynasty in Magadha, Mahapadma Nanda having overthrown the last Shishunaga king. The Haryankas came before the Shishunagas; the Mauryas and Shungas came after the Nandas.
t: Recall the Magadhan sequence: Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda, Maurya.
s: Which dynasty immediately preceded the Nanda Dynasty in Magadha?

x: Devabhuti was the last ruler of the Shunga dynasty. His minister Vasudeva founded the Kanva dynasty around 73 BC.
t: Discriminate the last Shunga from the first Kanva.
